answer_1.quote: Word-level error spans are widely used in machine translation (MT) evaluation to obtain robust and fine-grained estimates of translation quality.

answer_2.quote: We use the Surprisal of the predicted token t * , as negative log-probability log p(t * i |t <i ), and the Entropy H of the output distribution P N over vocabulary V , -|V | i=1 p(t i |t <i ) log 2 p(t i |t <i ), as simple metrics to quantify pointwise and full prediction uncertainty.

answer_4.quote: Importantly, we focus on texts with multiple human annotations to measure the impact of individual annotator preferences on metric performance, setting a 'human-level' baseline for the WQE task.
